primary_diagnosis_treated: Chronic kidney disease stage 4 with proteinuria and hypertension
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2–4 weeks to target 5 mg once daily as tolerated
medications.purpose: Reduce proteinuria, control blood pressure, and lower cardiovascular risk in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with proteinuria or hypertension; titrate to maximum tolerated dose

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises statin therapy for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.purpose: Additional blood‑pressure control if target <130/80 mmHg not achieved with ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: CKD BP targets in NG203; CCBs are safe in advanced CKD and can be added when ACE‑I insufficient

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily, adjust based on clinical response
medications.duration: As needed for volume overload — review monthly
medications.purpose: Treat symptomatic fluid overload (edema, weight gain) in CKD

treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily and titrate to 5 mg for proteinuric CKD and hypertension (NG203). Add atorvastatin 20 mg nightly for cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD risk‑equivalent). If BP remains above target, introduce amlodipine 5 mg daily. Prescribe furosemide 20 mg daily only if clinical signs of fluid overload appear. Avoid SGLT2 inhibitors, metformin, chronic NSAIDs, pioglitazone, and ACE‑I/ARB combination due to severe renal impairment and guideline contraindications. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, and BP according to NICE recommendations.
